decisions.statement: The `story-workflow.md` proposal will include a rule that `premerge-check` reads the code-review report and the finding files from the branch head with git, not from the folder it runs in, and reruns the gates in the story's checkout.
decisions.quote: The proposal says `premerge-check` reruns the gates "on the branch head", but it does not say where. Today `premerge-check` runs in the invocation checkout and reads everything from that folder: the story file, the gate results under `.current-work/`.

decisions.statement: The `story-workflow.md` proposal will be accepted and processed by the agent to update the primer and start the lector's structural pass.
decisions.quote: Shall I add the rule above and start with the primer?

decisions.statement: The `story-workflow.md` proposal will be updated with the rule about `premerge-check` and the primer will be generated.
decisions.quote: I added the rule to the "Checks at the merge" section, along with one completion criterion for it. A fresh agent is now writing the primer.

decisions.statement: The Summary will be revised to list what the proposal delivers, including one workflow, the three merge checks, the `story` field, the `dependency-check` hook, the split of the guardrail, and the deferred rule about which findings must be fixed.
decisions.quote: The Summary retells the primer. The lector proposes a new Summary that lists what the proposal delivers instead: one workflow, the three merge checks, the `story` field, the `dependency-check` hook, the split of the guardrail, and the deferred rule about which findings must be fixed.

decisions.statement: The gate list appears twice, but it will stay under step 4, and the merge check table will link to it.
decisions.quote: The gate list appears twice. It stays under step 4, and the merge check table links to it.

decisions.statement: The Bypass item will keep only the new fact that a human can still skip the hooks.
decisions.quote: The Bypass item keeps only the new fact, that a human can still bypass the hooks.

decisions.statement: The section 'Relation to the ownership proposal' will be removed, and its content will be merged into the Motivation paragraph.
decisions.quote: The section 'Relation to the ownership proposal' goes. Its quote joins the Motivation, and its sentence about the test-strategy agent moves under the gate list.

decisions.statement: The primer will lose the sentence 'The proposal has no open questions.'
decisions.quote: The primer loses the sentence 'The proposal has no open questions.'

decisions.statement: The Design sections now follow a specific order including the story workflow, two ways to drive it, findings naming their story, fast gates as pre-commit hooks, checks at the merge, and the git guardrail by path.
decisions.quote: The Design sections now run: The story workflow, Two ways to drive it, Findings name their story, Fast gates as pre-commit hooks, Checks at the merge, The git guardrail by path (items 1.1 and 1.2).

decisions.statement: The stakeholder recommends that story branches driven by hand should use the name `story/ST-NNNN` to ensure `premerge-check` checks them.
decisions.quote: I recommend that a story driven by hand also uses the name `story/ST-NNNN`.

decisions.statement: The dispatch process should be defined consistently, covering the entire lifecycle from start to end of a run, including cleanup.
decisions.quote: I recommend this order: 1. Put the story workflow on hold. 2. Write one proposal that defines the whole dispatch process, from the start of a run to its end, on both ways of driving it.

decisions.statement: The orchestrated mode requires that the `init` command creates a feature branch and a worktree, and refuses if any ledger has a non-terminal story or lacks a `test_command` in `docs/testing.yaml`.
decisions.quote: It refuses while any ledger anywhere has a non-terminal story (`_active_ledger`, :733-746). It also refuses when there is no `test_command` in `docs/testing.yaml`.

decisions.statement: In the orchestrated mode, `merge-story` must run on the invocation branch and handles conflicts by aborting and blocking the story.
decisions.quote: merge-story must run on the invocation branch (:1774-1985). In order, it: ... On a conflict it aborts and blocks the story.

decisions.statement:
The `premerge-check` command writes a marker file and reads gate results only for branches named `story/ST-
\d+`.
decisions.quote:
premerge-check writes `<toplevel>/.current-work/premerge-check-ok` with `branch=` and `head=` (premerge-check:87-96). It reads gate results only for branches named `story/ST-
\d+` (:170, :420-438).

decisions.statement: In the manual mode, there are no story branches, worktrees, ledger, or scripts, and the human handles all steps manually.
decisions.quote: The human creates `feature/<name>` from `dev` with `git checkout -b` or adopts the current branch. There are no story branches, worktrees, ledger, or scripts (bp:35-37, ia:157-158).

decisions.statement: The process has a defined start but no defined end.
decisions.quote: The process has a defined start and no defined end.

decisions.statement: Both ways of running a feature share one frame, with the human driving by hand starting from the feature branch.
decisions.quote: Settled: both ways share one frame. The person who drives by hand gets thorough guidance, which will become its own part of the proposal.

decisions.statement: The human merges the feature branch into `dev` on both ways after the check command passes.
decisions.quote: Settled: the human merges into `dev` on both ways, after the check command passes.

decisions.statement: The `dispatch close` command removes all run state and keeps no record beyond git history and the story files.
decisions.quote: Settled: `dispatch close` removes everything of the run and keeps no record beyond git history and the story files.

decisions.statement: A run ends either finished or dropped, with no run state remaining except unmerged branches that the human deletes.
decisions.quote: Settled: a run ends either finished or dropped. In both cases nothing of the run remains except unmerged branches, and the human deletes those.

decisions.statement: One run may be active per feature branch, with each run's ledger read only by its own branch.
decisions.quote: Settled: one run per feature branch. Every check that asks whether a run is active reads only the ledger of its own branch.

decisions.statement: The merge sets `done` on both ways, and the human who drives by hand merges with `dispatch merge-story`.
decisions.quote: Settled: the merge sets `done` on both ways, and the human who drives by hand merges with `dispatch merge-story`.

decisions.statement: The feature branch moves back to the commit before the failed merge, and the spec changes to match the code.
decisions.quote: Settled: the feature branch moves back to the commit before the failed merge, and the spec changes to match the code.

decisions.statement: The next wave starts only after the previous wave is closed, and by hand each story is a wave of its own.
decisions.quote: Settled: the next wave starts only after the previous wave is closed, and by hand each story is a wave of its own.

decisions.statement: The implementation agent runs the gates on both ways, and the developer agent never runs a gate script.
decisions.quote: Settled: the implementation agent runs the gates on both ways, and the developer agent never runs a gate script.

decisions.statement: Where a document and the code disagree with no design question behind it, the document changes to match the code.
decisions.quote: Recorded: where a document and the code disagree with no design question behind it, the document changes to match the code.

decisions.statement: The code review at the end of the feature and QA run inside the run, on the feature branch. The check before the merge into `dev` requires both to have finished with no open finding.
decisions.quote: yes. Development -> Test -> Code Review -> CRAP -> Mutaiton Testing -> QA and their fixing loops belong inside one run.

decisions.statement: The code review at the end of the feature stays and is part of the feature-level process.
decisions.quote: yes. Also: Security (either with the OWASP skill or as a deterministic gate in the pre-commits) scanning should happen per story.

decisions.statement: A deterministic scanner gate runs per story, configured per project, and the setup proposal will cover the tools.
decisions.quote: Recorded: a deterministic scanner gate per story, configured per project. Each project chooses whether to enable it and which scanners to run. The setup proposal will cover the tools.

decisions.statement: Drift sessions run at the close of each wave, not after each merge.
decisions.quote: I take "BZ" as B: the drift sessions run at the close of each wave.

decisions.statement: Every ledger field must have a command that reads it. Fields without a reader are removed, and the dispatch contract describes exactly the fields the code writes.
decisions.quote: Recorded: every ledger field must have a command that reads it. Fields without a reader go: `gate_results` because the gates are rerun, `closed` because the ledger's existence already says the run is active, and the audit requirement in the rules because the ledger is deleted at the close anyway.

decisions.statement: The agent asks at each point where a person decides, and runs the command on your yes.
decisions.quote: Settled: the agent asks at each point where a person decides, and runs the command on your yes.

decisions.statement: The ledger records the mode, and in a run driven by hand the guardrail asks you before each command that needs a person.
decisions.quote: Settled: the ledger records the mode, and in a run driven by hand the guardrail asks you before each command that needs a person.

decisions.statement: In a run driven by hand, the git guardrail refuses agents the commands that need a person, and you run those commands yourself. OpenCode gets the git guardrail as part of this work.
decisions.quote: Settled: in a run driven by hand, the git guardrail refuses agents the commands that need a person, and you run those commands yourself. OpenCode gets the git guardrail as part of this work.

decisions.statement: The proposal uses only the proposed vocabulary for terms.
decisions.quote: Settled: the proposal uses only that vocabulary.

decisions.statement: `dispatch close` also closes the old runs, and `--orphans` lists what has no ledger.
decisions.quote: Settled: `dispatch close` also closes the old runs, and `--orphans` lists what has no ledger.

decisions.statement: The proposal document is written and marked as a draft, with all twenty decisions presented in the present tense.
decisions.quote: I have written the proposal as `docs/proposals/run-lifecycle.md`, with `status: draft`.
